title: Space Race integration with the existing research and satellite systems
research_and_qualification: Research licenses hardware generations. Paid programme development qualifies hardware; successful prerequisite flights qualify operations. Neither research nor a failed mission grants a successful programme receipt.
first_generation: OLV 1965 remains sufficient for the original lunar architecture when heavy lift, docking and cislunar operations are independently qualified. OLV 1975 is not retroactively required for an Apollo-era landing.
advanced_generations: Modular stations, reusable spacecraft, deep-space infrastructure and Mars expeditions use later OLV generations. Relevant satellite payloads require GNSS, COMSAT or SPYSAT research. These are game-balance mappings of existing ten-year technology families, not literal equivalences between a rocket generation and a specific lift capacity.
contracts: Programmes using established contracted launch access or Interkosmos may use foreign launch services. The funded foreign-launch-partnership programme establishes that access without requiring an indigenous launcher first. It does not grant satellite payload research.
technology_probability_contribution: Each researched OLV generation above the mission minimum adds 0.5 percentage points departure probability, capped at 2 pp. Each relevant satellite generation above the initial payload generation adds 0.5 pp objective probability, capped at 2 pp. These are balance values; the recorded components and payload generation freeze at departure.
native_pilots: Seven satellite campaign types finance one pilot-asset entitlement on their first accepted flight. The native add_satellite_from_payload API retains orbital capacity, older-model replacement, ownership and target references. Queued payloads are preserved. The commissioned receipt is written only when the target-model counter increases; a rejected handover can retry on a later accepted flight without repeating national programme or research awards. No OLV inventory, full constellation or repeat free satellites are granted. Mission appropriation includes pilot procurement; the existing satellite system retains network operation and replacement.
special_project_access: In the 1970 human-player scenario, an established national space administration unlocks initial satellite and OLV research. Qualified orbital reconnaissance and OLV 1975 unlock initial ASAT research. Existing special-project routes remain in place for AI countries and other scenarios.
resource_policy: Satellite research, programmes, deployments and access treaties grant no raw production or resource-extraction multiplier. The existing resource-free satellite dynamic modifier is preserved. Obsolete GNSS resource calculations, model ranges and English tooltips are cleared. Existing saves have the final human-player resource variables reset during refresh.
historical_baselines: One-time migration fills missing first-generation 1965 knowledge for USA and SOV, OLV 1965 for France and COMSAT 1965 for Britain. It grants no deployed satellites, programme completions, prestige or later technology generations. Soviet navigation knowledge represents experimental Tsyklon hardware, not an operational global constellation.

precedents.example: Apollo 4 and Apollo 6 were uncrewed Saturn V qualification flights before the crewed lunar programme.
Transit entered operation in 1964 and depended on a network rather than a single satellite.
Early Bird was launched in 1965; ground networks and launch availability formed part of communications operations.
CORONA required repeated flight attempts before its first fully successful mission in 1960.
Zenit-2 completed Soviet reconnaissance flight tests in 1962-1963, supporting a pre-1970 first-generation imaging baseline.
France demonstrated independent orbital launch with Diamant-A in November 1965.
Britain's Skynet 1A communications satellite launched in November 1969 using US launch services.
Molniya-1 provided Soviet communications experiments from 1965.
Kosmos 192 was an early Tsyklon navigation prototype launched in 1967.

validation_limit: Native pilot transfer is covered by a modeled donor-API contract and static inspection of complete donor blocks. A live HOI4 and multiplayer test is still required for the full orbit, ASAT, treaty and save-cycle behavior.
international_launch_provider_update: Generic contracted-access receipts no longer bypass OLV research by themselves. Foreign-carriage catalogue programmes accept domestic OLV or a real consenting qualified provider; purchased launch partnership requires an actual provider. Capped launcher-generation chance uses the provider hardware when contracted. No research transfer, physical pad or inventory grant.
